 Sanjay Dutt pledges to make ‘Kaante 2’ in memory of Sanjay Gupta 
 By
 TNM (With ANI Inputs) 
 ✓
 31 October 2026, 2:02 pm 
 2 min read
 31 Oct 2026 
 ANI Photo | Sanjay Dutt pledges to make ‘Kaante 2’ in memory of Sanjay Gupta 
 Bollywood actor Sanjay Dutt has expressed his grief following the death of filmmaker Sanjay Gupta, with whom he shared a long-standing professional and personal relationship. Dutt paid tribute to Gupta as his “brother” and promised to realise their plans to create the sequel to the 2002 film Kaante , entitled Kaante 2 , in his memory.
 Posting pictures of the two together at various stages of their lives, Dutt wrote: “Gupts, my brother. I still cannot believe that you are gone. We have shared so much together, so many memories and so many years of friendship. You have always been family to me, and that will never change. I will miss you, our conversations and all the times we spent together. We were just discussing Kante 2 recently, I will make Kaante 2 your dream, in memory of you my brother, I will do everything for this dream of yours to come true, love you forever and always. Life will not be the same without you, brother. May God bless your soul.”

 Gupta was known for directing notable Bollywood crime thrillers including Kaante and Shootout at Lokhandwala . His work also included films such as Aatish: Feel the Fire , Jung , Khauff , Plan , Musafir , Zinda , and Shootout at Wadala . Kaante , released in 2002 starring Amitabh Bachchan, Suniel Shetty, Mahesh Manjrekar and Sanjay Dutt himself, was an unofficial adaptation of Quentin Tarantino’s Reservoir Dogs .
 Sanjay Gupta passed away on Saturday at the age of 57 following a head injury sustained at his residence, as confirmed by filmmaker Ashoke Pandit. Pandit described Gupta as “a wonderful narrator, full of life persona and a passionate filmmaker” and called his death “a great loss to our industry.”
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Gupta’s most recent directorial work was The Miranda Brothers , released in 2024, featuring Harshvardhan Rane and Meezaan Jafri. He also produced Visfot , starring Fardeen Khan and Riteish Deshmukh, and directed the 2021 film Mumbai Saga with John Abraham and Emraan Hashmi. His contributions largely centred on crime dramas and action films, through which he made a distinct mark on Hindi cinema.
 Further details surrounding his death are awaited.
